countries.name: Algeria
countries.summary: Algeria is Africa's largest country. The Mediterranean north (Algiers, Constantine and the Roman ruins at Timgad and Djemila) has hot summers and mild, wet winters, so spring and autumn are best. The Sahara (Djanet's Tassili n'Ajjer, the Hoggar mountains, the M'zab valley) is a desert destination from October to March.

regions.name: Mediterranean North
regions.description: Algiers, Oran, Constantine, Tlemcen and the Roman sites of Timgad, Djemila and Tipasa.

best.why: Mild, green spring for the casbah and the Roman ruins.
A warm sea and pleasant sightseeing.

worst.why: Rainy, cool weather.

shoulder.why: Spring showers.
A hot, humid summer and the domestic beach season.
Rains are returning.

recurringHolidays.name: Ramadan
recurringHolidays.approx: Moves about 11 days earlier each year
recurringHolidays.effect: Restaurants close by day.

recurringHolidays.name: Eid al-Fitr
recurringHolidays.effect: A national holiday.

prices.notes: Tourist visas need an invitation or tour booking, and some regions require police escorts.

regions.name: Algerian Sahara
regions.description: Djanet and the Tassili n'Ajjer, Tamanrasset and the Hoggar (Assekrem), Ghardaïa and the M'zab, and Timimoun.

best.why: Desert season: Tassili n'Ajjer rock art and dunes at 22–28 °C, with cold nights.

worst.why: 40 °C+ heat; many Saharan circuits shut down for summer.

shoulder.why: Heating up.
The heat is easing.

recurringHolidays.name: Ramadan
recurringHolidays.approx: Moves about 11 days earlier each year
recurringHolidays.effect: Restaurants close by day.

recurringHolidays.name: Eid al-Fitr
recurringHolidays.effect: A national holiday.

prices.notes: Deep-Sahara travel requires licensed agencies with 4x4s and guides.

countries.name: Angola
countries.summary: Angola is a big, little-visited country. The cool, dry 'cacimbo' season (mid-May to September) brings grey skies to the coast but sunny, dry weather inland, which suits road trips to the Kalandula Falls, the Serra da Leba road and the Namibe desert. The hot, rainy season peaks from February to April. Luanda is one of Africa's most expensive cities.
countries.splitReason: Few visitors travel beyond the main road-trip route, which follows one wet-and-dry pattern.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Luanda, Benguela and Lobito, Lubango and the Serra da Leba, Namibe and the Iona desert, and the Kalandula Falls.

best.why: Cacimbo season: dry and cool (24 °C), with sunny skies inland for road trips; the coast is often overcast.

worst.why: The heaviest rains and heat: roads in the interior flood and humidity is high.

shoulder.why: Hot, with the rains building inland; the coast stays sunny and Luanda's beaches are at their best.
The rains are ending.

prices.notes: Luanda hotels are expensive. Prices are lower in the provinces, but tourist infrastructure is thin.

countries.name: Benin
countries.summary: Benin is the birthplace of Vodun (voodoo). Ouidah hosts the national Vodun festival on 10 January, and the country also has Ganvié's stilt village, the royal palaces of Abomey and, in the north, Pendjari National Park. The dry season (mid-November to mid-March) is best. The south has rains from April to July and in October; the north has one rainy season from June to September. Check travel advice for the far north.
countries.splitReason: The southern sights and Pendjari share a dry-season window.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Cotonou, Ouidah, Ganvié, Porto-Novo, Grand-Popo, Abomey, Dassa and the north (Natitingou, Pendjari).

best.why: Dry season: sunny days, the Vodun festival in January and the best game viewing in Pendjari.

worst.why: The main rains: heavy storms and flooding in Cotonou.

shoulder.why: The little dry season on the coast.
The short rains.
Hot and humid, with the rains approaching.

recurringHolidays.name: Fête du Vodoun (Vodun Day)
recurringHolidays.effect: Ouidah fills up for the national Vodun festival; book well ahead.

prices.notes: Inexpensive. Ouidah guesthouses fill up for 10 January.

countries.name: Botswana
countries.summary: Botswana is a low-volume, high-cost safari country. The Okavango Delta floods in the middle of the dry season: water from Angola's rains peaks in the Delta from June to August, just as the land dries out. That, plus the huge elephant herds along the Chobe River, makes June to October the prime season. The green season (December to March) is hot and wet, with lower prices, newborn animals and the zebra migration in the Makgadikgadi Pans.
countries.splitReason: The Delta, Chobe and the Kalahari share the same summer-rain, dry-winter safari calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The Okavango Delta and Moremi, Chobe and Savuti, the Linyanti, the Makgadikgadi and Nxai Pans and the Central Kalahari.

best.why: Dry season with the Delta in flood: mokoro trips, huge elephant herds on the Chobe and the best game viewing.

worst.why: The heaviest rains: some camps and tracks close and game disperses into the thick bush.

shoulder.why: Rains begin; green-season rates and newborn antelope.
The rains end and the floodwaters reach the Delta from May; green-season rates linger and the Makgadikgadi zebra migration is under way.
Extreme heat (up to 40 °C), but superb predator sightings at the last waterholes.

prices.notes: Okavango and Chobe camps are all-inclusive and costly ($500–2,000 per person per night in peak season). Self-drive camping and lodges in Maun or Kasane are the budget route.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
countries.summary: Burkina Faso is known for its culture: the FESPACO film festival in Ouagadougou, the painted houses of Tiébélé and the Sindou Peaks near Banfora. The cool, dry season (November to mid-February) is best. March to May is very hot, and the rains fall from June to September. Government travel advice currently warns against travel to most of the country.
countries.splitReason: A landlocked Sahelian country with one wet-and-dry calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Ouagadougou, Bobo-Dioulasso, Banfora and the Sindou Peaks, and Tiébélé's painted villages.

best.why: Cool, dry season: warm days and comfortable evenings for the markets and festivals.

worst.why: Extreme heat of 40 °C+ and dusty skies.

shoulder.why: The rains: green countryside and cooler days, but muddy roads in August.
Heating up.

recurringHolidays.name: FESPACO film festival
recurringHolidays.effect: Africa's biggest film festival fills Ouagadougou's hotels.

prices.notes: Very cheap, but tourism is minimal because of insecurity. Check government travel advice.

countries.name: Burundi
countries.summary: Burundi sees very few tourists. Lake Tanganyika's beaches near Bujumbura and the Kibira forest are best in the June–September dry season.
countries.splitReason: Burundi is small, with one equatorial-highland calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Bujumbura and Lake Tanganyika, Gitega and Kibira National Park.

best.why: Dry season: Lake Tanganyika's beaches and the Kibira forest.

worst.why: The heaviest long rains; roads turn to mud and hikes get washed out.

shoulder.why: The short rains with sunny breaks.
The rains are easing.

prices.notes: There's little tourist infrastructure, so bring cash (US dollars).

countries.name: Cabo Verde
countries.summary: Cabo Verde is a ten-island Atlantic archipelago with a dry, breezy climate and 25–30 °C all year. From November to June it's sunny, with steady trade winds that make Sal and Boa Vista kitesurfing hotspots, and good hiking on green Santo Antão. From August to October it's hotter and humid, with occasional heavy showers, the calmest sea and turtles nesting. Harmattan dust can haze the skies from December to February.
countries.splitReason: The islands share one dry, trade-wind climate; the mountain islands are only a little greener.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Sal and Boa Vista's beaches, Santiago (Praia, Cidade Velha), Mindelo on São Vicente, the Santo Antão hiking trails and the Fogo volcano.

best.why: Winter sun at 25 °C; peak windsurfing and kitesurfing on Sal and Boa Vista.
Dry, sunny 26 °C days with steady trade winds; ideal for Santo Antão and Fogo hikes.

worst.why: The peak of the short rainy season: sticky humidity, heavy showers and occasional tropical storms.

shoulder.why: Hot, humid and calmer, with loggerhead turtles nesting on Boa Vista and Sal.
The rains are ending.

risks.note: Strong trade winds (great for kitesurfing, choppy for swimmers).

recurringHolidays.name: Carnival (Mindelo)
recurringHolidays.effect: Mindelo's carnival is the archipelago's biggest party; ferries and guesthouses fill up.

prices.notes: Sal and Boa Vista are all-inclusive resort islands. Santo Antão and Fogo have cheap guesthouses. Inter-island ferries are irregular.

countries.name: Cameroon
countries.summary: Cameroon is called 'Africa in miniature': beaches at Kribi and Limbe, the 4,040 m Mount Cameroon, the highlands of the Ring Road, rainforest at Dja and Campo Ma'an and, in the north, Waza's savanna. In the south, the dry season (December to February) is the time to go; the rains peak from July to October, and Douala is among the wettest cities in Africa. Check travel advice for the north and the anglophone regions.
countries.splitReason: Most visitors stay in the south and west, which share one wet-and-dry calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Douala and Yaoundé, Limbe and Mount Cameroon, Kribi and Campo Ma'an, the western highlands (Foumban, Bamenda) and Dja.

best.why: Dry season: sunny beach days at Kribi, the best Mount Cameroon climbs and passable forest roads.

worst.why: The heaviest rains: Douala and Limbe get 700 mm a month and roads turn to mud.

shoulder.why: The rains are increasing, with hot and humid weather.
The rains are easing.

recurringHolidays.name: Mount Cameroon Race of Hope
recurringHolidays.effect: Crowds gather in Buea for the mountain race.

prices.notes: Mid-range hotels in Kribi and Limbe. A guide is mandatory for Mount Cameroon.

countries.name: Central African Republic
countries.summary: The Central African Republic is home to Dzanga-Sangha, one of Africa's best places to see western lowland gorillas and forest elephants (at the Dzanga Bai clearing). The dry season (December to March) is best for reaching the park. Government travel advice warns against all travel to most of the country, so check it first.
countries.splitReason: Tourism is effectively limited to Dzanga-Sangha, which follows one rainforest calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Bangui and the Dzanga-Sangha reserve in the south-west.

best.why: Dry season: drier forest trails for gorilla tracking and easier access to Bayanga.

worst.why: Heavy rains: forest tracks flood and access is very difficult.

shoulder.why: The rains return.
The rains are easing.

prices.notes: Access to Dzanga-Sangha is usually by charter flight or via Cameroon or Congo. Check government travel advice and insurance.

countries.name: Chad
countries.summary: Chad has two remarkable sights: Zakouma National Park, a conservation success with huge buffalo herds and elephants, and the sandstone arches and gueltas of the Ennedi Plateau. Both are dry-season only. Zakouma opens from December to June, and its best game viewing is from March to May, when water is scarce. The rains (June to October) close the parks and the roads. Check travel advice.
countries.splitReason: Travel is limited to dry-season trips to Zakouma and Ennedi, which follow one calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: N'Djamena, Zakouma National Park, the Ennedi Plateau and Abéché.

best.why: The cool, dry season: Zakouma's animals gather at the waterholes and the Ennedi Plateau is accessible.

worst.why: The rains: Zakouma closes and the roads become impassable.

shoulder.why: Extreme 45 °C heat, but the best game viewing in Zakouma (until May).
The rains are over, but it's still hot.

prices.notes: Zakouma's camps (Camp Nomade, Tinga) are run by African Parks and book out early. Most travel is by charter flight.

countries.name: Comoros
countries.summary: The Comoros are three volcanic islands between Madagascar and Mozambique, with almost no tourism: Grande Comore with the Karthala volcano, wild Mohéli with nesting turtles and whale sharks, and Anjouan with ylang-ylang plantations. The coolest, driest months are July to November. December to April is hot, humid and wet, with cyclone risk. Most of the population is Muslim, so Ramadan affects opening hours.
countries.splitReason: Three small islands with the same tropical cyclone-season pattern.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Moroni and Grande Comore, the Karthala volcano, Mohéli Marine Park and Anjouan.

best.why: The driest, coolest months: sunny 27 °C days for climbing Karthala, turtle-watching on Mohéli and diving.

worst.why: Hot, humid cyclone season with torrential rain.

shoulder.why: Cooler, but showers persist.
Rains building and very humid.

recurringHolidays.name: Ramadan
recurringHolidays.approx: Moves about 11 days earlier each year
recurringHolidays.effect: Restaurants close by day.

prices.notes: Very little tourist infrastructure; inter-island flights and boats are irregular.

countries.name: Côte d'Ivoire
countries.summary: Côte d'Ivoire combines Abidjan's lively Plateau and nightlife, the colonial town of Grand-Bassam, the lagoon beaches of Assinie and the giant basilica of Yamoussoukro. The south has two rainy seasons: the main one from May to July and a short one from October to November. December to March is dry, hot and sunny, and the best time to visit. The north (Korhogo, Comoé) has a single, Sahel-style rainy season.
countries.splitReason: Most visitors stay in the south (Abidjan, Grand-Bassam, Assinie, Yamoussoukro), which follows one calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Abidjan, Grand-Bassam, Assinie, Yamoussoukro, San-Pédro and Sassandra, Man's mountains and Korhogo in the north.

best.why: Dry season: hot, sunny 31 °C days and calm lagoon beaches.

worst.why: The main rainy season: heavy daily downpours and flooding in Abidjan.

shoulder.why: The 'little dry season': cloudy and cooler, with fewer rains.
The short rains.
Hot and humid, with rains building.

risks.note: Flash floods and landslides in Abidjan.
Dangerous Atlantic currents; swim only where locals do.

prices.notes: Abidjan is one of West Africa's pricier cities. Assinie beach hotels fill at weekends with city residents.

countries.name: Djibouti
countries.summary: Djibouti is one of the world's hottest countries. Visit from November to January to snorkel with whale sharks in the Gulf of Tadjoura and see the otherworldly Lac Assal and Lac Abbé. Summer is dangerously hot.
countries.splitReason: Djibouti is small, with one hot desert-coast climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Djibouti City, the Gulf of Tadjoura, Lac Assal and Lac Abbé.

best.why: Whale sharks in the Gulf of Tadjoura (November–January), at a cooler 29 °C.

worst.why: Brutal 40–45 °C heat.

shoulder.why: Warming up.
The heat is easing.

risks.note: Among the hottest places on earth.

prices.notes: Expensive, as it's a military-base economy.

countries.name: DR Congo
countries.summary: Most visitors to DR Congo head to the east: mountain gorillas in Virunga National Park, an overnight on the rim of the Nyiragongo volcano above its lava lake, and eastern lowland gorillas at Kahuzi-Biega. The main dry season (June to mid-September) and a shorter spell from December to February make for easier treks. Security in the east changes quickly and parks sometimes close, so check government travel advice and Virunga's official site.
countries.splitReason: Visitors mostly go to the eastern highlands (Virunga, Kahuzi-Biega), which follow one two-season calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Goma, Virunga and Nyiragongo, Bukavu and Kahuzi-Biega, plus Kinshasa.

best.why: The main dry season: easier gorilla treks in Virunga and Kahuzi-Biega and clearer views from Nyiragongo.

worst.why: The long rains: slippery forest trails, muddy roads and flooding in Kinshasa.

shoulder.why: A shorter dry spell in the east; hot and humid in Kinshasa.
The short rains.
The rains are building.

prices.notes: Gorilla permits in Virunga cost about $400. Book through the official park site, which also runs the lodges.

countries.name: Egypt
countries.summary: Egypt is almost rainless. The Nile Valley (Cairo, Luxor, Aswan) is a winter destination: November to February is 23–28 °C and perfect for temples and Nile cruises, while summer reaches 40–45 °C in Luxor and Aswan. The Red Sea resorts (Hurghada, Sharm el-Sheikh, Dahab) are good year-round, best in spring and autumn. Alexandria and the Mediterranean coast are a summer escape for Egyptians.

regions.name: Cairo & the Nile Valley
regions.description: Cairo and Giza, Luxor, Aswan, Abu Simbel and the Nile cruise route, plus the western desert oases (Siwa, the White Desert).

best.why: Warm, dry 23–28 °C: perfect for the Valley of the Kings, Karnak and Nile cruises.

worst.why: 40–45 °C in Luxor and Aswan.

shoulder.why: Hot afternoons and khamsin dust storms (March–April).
The heat is easing.

recurringHolidays.effect: Site hours shorten; iftar evenings are festive.

regions.name: Red Sea & Sinai
regions.description: Hurghada, El Gouna, Marsa Alam, Sharm el-Sheikh, Dahab, Saint Catherine and Mt Sinai.

best.why: A warm sea, sunny days and perfect diving.
The sea at 27 °C, with calm conditions.

worst.why: The hottest weeks (35–40 °C in Sharm) and peak family-holiday prices.

shoulder.why: Pleasant 21–24 °C winter sun, but the sea is 21–22 °C (wetsuit needed) and it's breezy.
Hot, with good diving.
Still hot, with a very warm sea.

recurringHolidays.approx: Moves about 11 days earlier each year
recurringHolidays.effect: Site hours shorten; iftar evenings are festive.

recurringHolidays.effect: Peak prices in Luxor and on the Red Sea.

regions.name: Alexandria & the Mediterranean
regions.description: Alexandria, El Alamein and the North Coast (Sahel), and Marsa Matrouh.

best.why: Mild, sunny days on the corniche.
A warm sea after the Egyptian summer crowds.

worst.why: Winter storms (nawas) bring rain and rough seas.

shoulder.why: Cool spring.
The Egyptian summer peak on the North Coast.
Storms are beginning.

recurringHolidays.approx: Moves about 11 days earlier each year
recurringHolidays.effect: Site hours shorten; iftar evenings are festive.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak prices in Luxor and on the Red Sea.

prices.notes: North Coast resorts are packed with Cairenes from July to August.

countries.name: Equatorial Guinea
countries.summary: Equatorial Guinea is split between Bioko Island (Malabo, with its colonial architecture, and the black-sand beaches and turtle nesting at Ureca) and the mainland, Río Muni (Bata and Monte Alén). The driest months on Bioko are December to February, which is also turtle-nesting season. From March to November it's hot, humid and often rainy, wettest in September and October. Visitor visas and permits are bureaucratic.
countries.splitReason: A small country where Bioko and the mainland follow a similar equatorial calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Malabo and Bioko Island (Ureca, Moka, Luba), Bata and the mainland.

best.why: The driest months on Bioko, with sea turtles nesting on the Ureca beaches.

worst.why: The wettest weeks: heavy rain and overcast skies.

shoulder.why: Hot, humid and frequently rainy.
The rains are easing.

prices.notes: Expensive, with few tourist facilities. Photography permits may be required.

countries.name: Eritrea
countries.summary: Asmara's art-deco streets enjoy spring-like weather much of the year. The coast at Massawa is pleasant in winter and brutally hot in summer. Travel permits are needed outside Asmara.
countries.splitReason: Eritrea is small, and the Asmara highlands and the Massawa coast share the same dry season.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Asmara, Keren, Massawa and the Dahlak Islands.

best.why: Dry, sunny highlands, with the Massawa coast warm rather than scorching.

worst.why: Massawa passes 40 °C, and the highlands have their rains.

shoulder.why: Hot on the coast.
The rains are ending.

prices.notes: Bring cash. Travel permits for each region are issued in Asmara.

countries.name: Eswatini
countries.summary: Eswatini (formerly Swaziland) is a small kingdom with wildlife reserves (Hlane, Mkhaya, Mlilwane), mountain hiking at Malolotja and lively cultural festivals. The dry winter (May to September) is best for game viewing and includes the Umhlanga Reed Dance in late August or early September. Summers are hot and humid, with heavy thunderstorms.
countries.splitReason: A small country where the reserves and valleys share one summer-rain calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Mbabane, the Ezulwini Valley and Mlilwane, Hlane, Mkhaya, Malolotja and Lobamba.

best.why: Dry winter: good game viewing, sunny 20 °C days and the Umhlanga Reed Dance.

worst.why: Hot, humid lowveld with heavy thunderstorms.

shoulder.why: The rains are ending and the landscape is lush.
Heating up, with the first storms.

recurringHolidays.name: Umhlanga Reed Dance
recurringHolidays.effect: A huge national ceremony; accommodation fills up.

recurringHolidays.name: Incwala
recurringHolidays.effect: The sacred kingship ceremony.

prices.notes: Often combined with Kruger. Big Game Parks reserves offer rest camps and lodges.

countries.name: Ethiopia
countries.summary: Ethiopia's historic north (Lalibela, Gondar, Aksum) and the Simien Mountains are best in the dry season from October to February, when the land is green after the rains and the Timkat (January) and Meskel (September) festivals take place. The main kiremt rains (June–September) bring mud and cloud. Some regions carry travel warnings, so check current advice.
countries.splitReason: The main circuit is in the highlands, which share one calendar; the Danakil and Omo lowlands are hotter but have the same dry season.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: The whole country: Addis Ababa, Lalibela, Gondar, the Simien Mountains, Aksum, Bahir Dar, the Danakil, the Omo Valley and Harar.

best.why: Dry and green after the rains, with the Meskel and Timkat festivals, Simien treks and Lalibela's churches.

worst.why: Main rains (kiremt): muddy, with cloud over the Simien and disrupted flights in the north.

shoulder.why: Hot lowlands and the short belg rains; the Danakil is too hot by May.
Meskel season, with flowers in bloom.

recurringHolidays.name: Timkat (Epiphany)
recurringHolidays.effect: Lalibela and Gondar hotels sell out.

recurringHolidays.name: Meskel
recurringHolidays.effect: The Finding of the True Cross, with huge bonfires.

recurringHolidays.name: Genna (Christmas)
recurringHolidays.effect: A pilgrimage to Lalibela.

prices.notes: Ethiopian Airlines gives domestic flight discounts if you fly in with them.

countries.name: Gabon
countries.summary: About 88% of Gabon is rainforest, and 13 national parks protect it: Loango, where elephants walk the beaches and hippos surf, the forests of Lopé and the turtle beaches of Pongara. The long dry season (June to mid-September) is cooler and overcast, the best time for forest trails and humpback whales off Loango. The wettest months are October and November, then March to May.
countries.splitReason: The parks and Libreville share one equatorial two-season calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Libreville, Pongara, Loango, Lopé, Ivindo, Lambaréné, Port-Gentil and Franceville.

best.why: The long dry season: cooler, overcast days, humpback whales off Loango and easier forest trails.

worst.why: The wettest months: torrential downpours and flooded park tracks.

shoulder.why: The short dry spell: hot and humid, with leatherback turtles nesting at Pongara.
The second heavy rains: hot and humid, with forest elephants in Lopé.
The rains are returning.

prices.notes: Expensive. Park lodges (Loango, Lopé) are mostly packages with transfers by plane or boat.

countries.name: Ghana
countries.summary: Ghana is one of West Africa's easiest countries to travel: Accra's arts scene, the slave castles at Cape Coast and Elmina, the Kakum canopy walk, Ashanti culture in Kumasi and elephants at Mole National Park. The dry season (mid-November to March) is best, though Harmattan dust hazes the skies from December to February. The coast has its main rains from April to June and minor rains in September and October. December is peak diaspora season in Accra.
countries.splitReason: The coast, Kumasi and Mole are close enough to share a dry-season window.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Accra, Cape Coast and Elmina, Kakum, Busua, Kumasi, the Volta region and Mole National Park.

best.why: Dry season: sunny days, the best game viewing at Mole and easy road travel (with Harmattan haze from December to February).

worst.why: The main rains on the coast: heavy downpours, flooding in Accra and muddy roads.

shoulder.why: The coast's cooler, drier spell, though the north is at its wettest.
The minor rains on the coast.
Hot and sticky as the rains begin.

recurringHolidays.name: December in Ghana
recurringHolidays.effect: Diaspora homecoming season, with concerts and festivals; Accra hotels and flights peak.

recurringHolidays.name: PANAFEST & Emancipation Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Cape Coast heritage events.

prices.notes: Good-value guesthouses on the coast. Accra prices jump in December.

countries.name: Guinea
countries.summary: Guinea has the Fouta Djallon highlands (waterfalls, hiking and cool plateaux), the Îles de Los off Conakry and the forests near Mount Nimba. The coast is one of the wettest places in West Africa: Conakry gets more than 1,000 mm of rain in July alone. Travel in the dry season (mid-November to March), ideally right after the rains, when the waterfalls are still full.
countries.splitReason: Travel follows one wet-and-dry calendar; the Fouta Djallon is just cooler.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Conakry and the Îles de Los, the Fouta Djallon highlands (Dalaba, Labé, Pita), Kindia and the forests near Mount Nimba.

best.why: Dry season: sunny days, cool highland nights and full waterfalls in November and December.

worst.why: Torrential rains (Conakry gets more than 1,000 mm in July) and impassable roads.

shoulder.why: Hot and humid, with the rains arriving.
The rains are easing and the Fouta Djallon waterfalls are at their fullest.

prices.notes: Very few tourist facilities outside Conakry; roads are rough.

countries.name: Guinea-Bissau
countries.summary: Guinea-Bissau's highlight is the Bijagós archipelago: 88 islands of mangroves, saltwater hippos, nesting turtles and matriarchal island cultures. The dry season (mid-November to mid-May) is the time to go. From July to September the rains are torrential and boats to the islands are limited.
countries.splitReason: A small country with one tropical wet-and-dry calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Bissau, the Bijagós archipelago (Bubaque, Orango, João Vieira), Varela and Cacheu.

best.why: Dry season: sunny 31 °C days and calm sea crossings to the Bijagós.

worst.why: Torrential rains, rough crossings and closed island lodges.

shoulder.why: Hot and humid, with the rains arriving.
The rains are easing; turtles nesting on Poilão from August to November.

prices.notes: Bijagós lodges are mostly fishing camps. Boats from Bissau run a few times a week.

countries.name: Kenya
countries.summary: Kenya has two dry seasons that make the best safari months: July to October, when the Great Migration's river crossings happen in the Masai Mara, and January to February, when it's hot and green with great game viewing. The long rains (April–May) make tracks muddy and close some camps. The coast (Diani, Watamu, Lamu) is best from October to March, when the sea is calm.

regions.name: Safari Parks & Highlands
regions.description: Nairobi, the Masai Mara, Amboseli, Samburu, Lake Nakuru and Naivasha, Laikipia, Mt Kenya and Tsavo.

best.why: Great Migration river crossings in the Masai Mara and dry-season game viewing.
The short dry season: great game viewing and fewer vehicles.

worst.why: Long rains: muddy tracks, with some camps closed.

shoulder.why: Dry season beginning, before the peak prices.
The short rains (November) bring lush scenery and lower prices.
Festive peak.
Hot, with the rains approaching.

recurringHolidays.name: Great Migration in the Mara
recurringHolidays.effect: Mara Conservancy camps peak in price.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak lodge and coast prices.

prices.notes: Mara conservancy camps are all-inclusive. Park fees are $100–200 per person per day.

regions.name: Kenyan Coast
regions.description: Mombasa, Diani Beach, Watamu and Malindi, Kilifi and the Lamu archipelago.

best.why: Dry seasons: a calm sea, kitesurfing (December–March) and whale sharks.

worst.why: Long rains: humid with a rough sea, and many hotels close.

shoulder.why: Hot, with the rains approaching.
The breezy kusi monsoon brings seaweed on the beaches, plus humpback whales (July–October).

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak lodge and coast prices.

prices.notes: Lamu is car-free, with dhow trips. Diani is the main resort strip.

countries.name: Lesotho
countries.summary: Lesotho is a mountain kingdom where every point lies above 1,400 m. Autumn (March to May) and spring (September to November) are best for hiking, pony trekking and the Sani Pass. Winter brings freezing nights, snow on the passes and skiing at Afriski. Summer is green but has daily thunderstorms that wash out dirt roads.
countries.splitReason: A small, entirely highland country with one mountain climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Maseru, the Sani Pass, Semonkong and the Maletsunyane Falls, Malealea, Katse Dam and the Afriski ski area.

best.why: Autumn: clear, dry days of 20 °C for hiking and pony trekking.
Spring: warm days and wildflowers, before the summer storms.

worst.why: The heaviest summer rains, with daily thunderstorms and flash floods on mountain roads.

shoulder.why: Winter: freezing nights (−10 °C in the highlands), snow closing the passes and skiing at Afriski.
Green and warm, with afternoon storms.

risks.note: Snow closes the Sani Pass and highland roads.

prices.notes: A 4x4 is required for the Sani Pass. Rustic lodges and community trekking are inexpensive.

countries.name: Liberia
countries.summary: Liberia has Robertsport's surf breaks, the rainforest of Sapo National Park and a long, empty coastline. The dry season (mid-November to April) is the time to go, with the best surf from April to October. The rainy season (May to October) is among the wettest anywhere, and many roads become impassable.
countries.splitReason: A small country with one tropical wet-and-dry calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Monrovia, Robertsport, Buchanan, Harper and Sapo National Park.

best.why: Dry season: sunny days, passable roads and calm beaches.

worst.why: Very heavy rains (950 mm in June in Monrovia) and roads turned to mud.

shoulder.why: Hot and humid, with the rains starting; good surf.
Rains easing.

prices.notes: Monrovia hotels are expensive for the quality. Robertsport has simple surf lodges.

countries.name: Libya
countries.summary: Many governments advise against all travel to Libya, so check current advice. Leptis Magna and Sabratha are among the finest Roman ruins anywhere. The coast is best in spring and autumn, and the Saharan oases such as Ghadames in winter.
countries.splitReason: Travel is very limited, and Tripoli and the Roman cities share one Mediterranean calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Tripoli, Leptis Magna, Sabratha, Cyrene and Ghadames.

best.why: Mild, sunny spring at the Roman ruins.
Pleasant autumn on the coast.

worst.why: Hot, with desert winds (ghibli).

shoulder.why: Cool, with some rain.
Getting hot.
The heat is easing.

prices.notes: There's no tourist infrastructure to speak of, and security dominates costs.

countries.name: Madagascar
countries.summary: Madagascar is a mini-continent of lemurs, baobabs and limestone tsingy. The dry season (April to November) is the time to go. April to June is green after the rains; September to November is warm, with baby lemurs and the best wildlife. The cyclone season (January to March) washes out roads and closes the Tsingy de Bemaraha. The highlands get cold at night in July and August, and humpback whales gather off Île Sainte-Marie from July to September.

regions.name: Highlands & Eastern Rainforests
regions.description: Antananarivo, Andasibe, Ranomafana, Antsirabe, Fianarantsoa, Isalo and Île Sainte-Marie.

best.why: Dry after the rains: green forests and comfortable 20–24 °C highland days.
Warm, dry days and baby lemurs in Ranomafana and Andasibe; humpbacks off Sainte-Marie until September.

worst.why: Cyclone season and heavy rain: unpaved roads become impassable.

shoulder.why: Cool winter (6 °C nights in Tana) but dry; humpback whale season off Île Sainte-Marie.
The rains are beginning.
The rains are ending; roads are still muddy.

risks.note: Road washouts on RN7 and the east coast.

prices.notes: Most visitors hire a car with a driver ($60–90 a day). Domestic flights are expensive and often rescheduled.

regions.name: West & North Coast
regions.description: Nosy Be and Nosy Komba, Antsiranana (Diego Suarez) and Ankarana, the Tsingy de Bemaraha, Morondava's Avenue of the Baobabs and Toliara (Ifaty, Anakao).

best.why: Dry season: sunny 28–30 °C days, a calm sea around Nosy Be and the Tsingy de Bemaraha open.

worst.why: Cyclones and heavy rain: the Tsingy de Bemaraha and the Morondava roads close.

shoulder.why: Hot and humid as the rains start; whale sharks off Nosy Be (October–December).
The rains are ending; the Tsingy reopens from late April or May.

risks.note: Western dirt roads to the Tsingy close.

prices.notes: Nosy Be has the most resort-style hotels. The Tsingy de Bemaraha is reached by 4x4 from Morondava (1–2 days).

countries.name: Malawi
countries.summary: Malawi is dominated by Lake Malawi, a freshwater 'inland sea' with beaches, cichlid snorkelling and kayaking. The cool, dry season (May to September) is the most comfortable time for the lake and for game in Liwonde and Majete. October and November are very hot but good for wildlife. The rains (December to March) bring humidity and muddy roads.
countries.splitReason: A small country whose lake and parks share one tropical wet-and-dry calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Lilongwe and Blantyre, Lake Malawi (Cape Maclear, Nkhata Bay, Likoma), Liwonde and Majete, Zomba, Mount Mulanje and the Nyika Plateau.

best.why: Cool, dry season: sunny 25 °C days on the lake, clear water and good game viewing in Liwonde.

worst.why: The rains: heavy downpours, high humidity and washed-out roads.

shoulder.why: Very hot before the rains, but the lake is at its clearest for snorkelling and the game viewing is excellent.
Lush after the rains, with roads still muddy.

risks.note: Roads flood and some lodges close.

prices.notes: One of Africa's cheaper safari-and-beach countries. Lakeshore backpacker lodges cost $15–40 a night.

countries.name: Mali
countries.summary: Mali has some of West Africa's greatest sights: the mud mosque of Djenné, Dogon Country and Timbuktu. Government travel advice currently warns against all or most travel, so check it before planning. In general the cool, dry season (November to February) is the best time. April to June is extremely hot, and the rains (July to October) green the Sahel and raise the Niger River.
countries.splitReason: The visitor sites along the Niger share one Sahelian calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Bamako, Ségou, Djenné, Mopti, Dogon Country (Bandiagara) and Timbuktu.

best.why: Cool, dry season: 30 °C days and cool nights; Djenné and Dogon Country at their most comfortable.

worst.why: Extreme 40–45 °C heat before the rains.

shoulder.why: Rainy season: green, but roads flood; the Niger is high enough for river boats from August.
Heating up fast.

recurringHolidays.effect: Daytime services are limited.

recurringHolidays.effect: A major festival; transport is busy.

prices.notes: Tourism has largely collapsed because of insecurity. Check government travel advice and insurance cover.

countries.name: Mauritania
countries.summary: Mauritania is almost all Sahara. The cool season (November to mid-March) is the only comfortable time for the Adrar circuit (Chinguetti, Ouadane, Terjit), the iron-ore train and the birds of the Banc d'Arguin. From May to September interior temperatures pass 45 °C. Check government travel advice, because large areas of the east and north are advised against.
countries.splitReason: Almost the entire country is Saharan, with one desert calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Nouakchott, Nouadhibou and the iron-ore train, the Adrar (Atar, Chinguetti, Ouadane, Terjit) and the Banc d'Arguin.

best.why: Cool season: warm days and cold nights for the Adrar's dunes and the ancient libraries of Chinguetti; migratory birds on the Banc d'Arguin.

worst.why: 45 °C heat and sandstorms; the desert circuits shut down.

shoulder.why: Heating up, with sand-laden winds.
The heat is easing.

recurringHolidays.name: Ramadan
recurringHolidays.approx: Moves about 11 days earlier each year
recurringHolidays.effect: Daytime services are limited.

prices.notes: Adrar guesthouses (auberges) are simple. Most visitors use a local agency with a 4x4 and driver.

countries.name: Mauritius
countries.summary: Mauritius is warm all year. The best spells are April to June and September to early December, which are sunny, less humid and calm. Summer (December to April) is hot and humid, with cyclone risk peaking from January to March. The winter months (June to September) are drier but windy and cooler (24 °C), with chilly evenings and a choppy east coast, which is ideal for kitesurfing.
countries.splitReason: A small island with one tropical climate (the east coast is a little windier).

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Port Louis, Grand Baie, Flic en Flac and Tamarin, Le Morne, Belle Mare and Île aux Cerfs, Chamarel and the Black River Gorges, Mahébourg and Rodrigues.

best.why: Sunny, less humid weather, with a warm sea after the cyclone season.
Warm, dry and sunny, with calm seas and great diving.

worst.why: Peak cyclone season: hot, humid and stormy.

shoulder.why: Cool, windy winter: great kitesurfing in the south-east, chilly evenings and occasional showers.
Hot, humid festive peak with the highest prices.
The cyclone risk is fading.

risks.note: Tropical cyclones; resorts follow class 1–4 warnings.

prices.notes: Mostly a resort destination. Guesthouses in Grand Baie and Flic en Flac cost $60–120 a night.

countries.name: Morocco
countries.summary: Morocco has three faces. The Atlantic coast (Essaouira, Agadir) stays mild all year, cooled by the ocean. The imperial cities and the Atlas (Marrakech, Fes, Toubkal) are best in spring and autumn, but hit 40 °C in summer and have cold nights in winter. The Sahara around Merzouga is a desert-camp destination from October to April. Ramadan shifts by about 11 days a year, which changes opening hours.

regions.name: Atlantic & Mediterranean Coast
regions.description: Essaouira, Agadir and Taghazout, Rabat, Casablanca, Tangier, Asilah and Chefchaouen in the Rif.

best.why: Sunny 20–24 °C days, good surf and blue-washed Chefchaouen in spring.
Warm sea and calm, clear weather.

worst.why: The rainiest, coolest weeks, with Atlantic storms (though Agadir stays sunny).

shoulder.why: Spring blooms and big surf.
Windy in Essaouira and busy with Moroccan holidaymakers, with the sea cool at 20 °C.
Showers returning.

regions.name: Imperial Cities & the Atlas
regions.description: Marrakech, Fes, Meknes and Volubilis, the High Atlas (Imlil, Toubkal), Aït Benhaddou, Ouarzazate and the Dades and Todra gorges.

best.why: Warm 25–30 °C with blossoms and snow-capped Atlas views; Toubkal treks from May.
Pleasant autumn for the souks and mountain villages.

worst.why: Marrakech hits 38–42 °C and the Fes medina is stifling.

shoulder.why: Sunny 18–20 °C days but cold 5 °C nights and snow in the Atlas, with skiing at Oukaïmeden; Christmas crowds in Marrakech.

regions.name: Sahara (Merzouga & Zagora)
regions.description: Merzouga and Erg Chebbi, Zagora and Erg Chigaga, and the Draa Valley.

best.why: Warm days and cool nights for camel treks and desert camps.
Mild spring days in the dunes.

countries.name: Mozambique
countries.summary: Mozambique has 2,500 km of Indian Ocean coast. In the south (Tofo, Vilankulo and the Bazaruto archipelago) the dry, sunny winter from May to October brings 26 °C days, humpback whales and year-round whale sharks and manta rays. The north (Pemba, the Quirimbas, Ilha de Moçambique) has a similar dry season but a stronger rainy and cyclone season from December to March. Check government travel advice before visiting Cabo Delgado province in the far north, where there has been an insurgency.

regions.name: Southern Coast & Bazaruto
regions.description: Maputo, Ponta do Ouro, Tofo and Inhambane, Vilankulo and the Bazaruto archipelago, Beira and Gorongosa.

best.why: Dry, sunny 26 °C days, humpback whales (June–October), and great diving with mantas and whale sharks.

worst.why: Peak cyclone season, with heavy rain and high humidity.

shoulder.why: Hot and humid as the rains begin; South African holidaymakers fill Ponta do Ouro in December.
The cyclone risk fades and it's still hot, with warm water.

risks.note: Tropical cyclones from the Mozambique Channel.

recurringHolidays.name: South African school holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Ponta do Ouro and the southern beaches fill up with South African visitors.

prices.notes: Tofo is a backpacker and diver hub. Bazaruto island lodges are luxury-only ($500+). Malaria precautions are advised.

regions.name: Northern Coast & Quirimbas
regions.description: Ilha de Moçambique, Nampula and Nacala, Pemba, Ibo and the Quirimbas archipelago, and Lake Niassa.

best.why: Dry season: sunny 28 °C days, a calm, clear sea and the best diving.

worst.why: The rainy season, with cyclone risk and humid, sticky heat.

shoulder.why: The rains are ending and everything is lush.
Hot and humid, with the first rains.

recurringHolidays.name: South African school holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Ponta do Ouro and the southern beaches fill up with South African visitors.

prices.notes: Ilha de Moçambique has charming guesthouses. Check current travel advice before travelling to Cabo Delgado (Pemba and the Quirimbas).

countries.name: Namibia
countries.summary: Namibia is one of the driest countries on Earth and a classic self-drive destination. The dry winter (May to October) is best: Etosha's animals crowd the waterholes, skies are clear for the Sossusvlei dunes and days are a comfortable 25 °C, though desert nights get close to freezing. November to February is very hot, with the summer rains arriving from December. Swakopmund on the coast stays cool and foggy all year.
countries.splitReason: The whole country shares one desert calendar: a dry winter and a hot summer with rains.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Windhoek, Sossusvlei and the Namib dunes, Swakopmund, Etosha, Damaraland, the Skeleton Coast, Fish River Canyon and the Caprivi Strip.

best.why: Dry season: clear skies over Sossusvlei, animals gathered at Etosha's waterholes and comfortable 25 °C days.

worst.why: Heat and the summer rains: Etosha's animals disperse and gravel roads and river crossings can flood.

shoulder.why: Very hot (35 °C+) with the first storms; Sossusvlei is scorching by midday.
Green landscapes after the rains, warm days and fewer visitors.

risks.note: Desert temperatures above 40 °C in the Namib and the south.
Flash floods in dry riverbeds on gravel roads.

prices.notes: Most visitors rent a 4x4 with rooftop tents ($100–200 a day). Lodges near Sossusvlei and Etosha book out in July–October. Malaria precautions are advised in the far north in the rainy season.

countries.name: Niger
countries.summary: Niger is mostly Sahara and Sahel: Agadez's mud minaret, the Aïr Mountains and the Ténéré desert. The cool, dry months (November to mid-February) are the only comfortable time. Government travel advice currently warns against most travel. April to June is extremely hot, and the short rains (July to September) bring the Tuareg and Wodaabe gatherings near Ingall.
countries.splitReason: The whole country shares one Sahelian-desert calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Niamey and the Niger River, Agadez, Zinder, the Aïr Mountains and the Ténéré desert.

best.why: The cool, dry season: warm days, cold desert nights and clear skies.

worst.why: Extreme heat of 42–46 °C before the rains.

shoulder.why: Short rainy season: humid and green in the south; the Cure Salée nomad gathering in September.
Heating up quickly.

recurringHolidays.approx: Moves about 11 days earlier each year
recurringHolidays.effect: Daytime services are limited.

prices.notes: Very limited tourism infrastructure. Check government travel advice and insurance cover.

countries.name: Nigeria
countries.summary: Nigeria is Africa's most populous country and a cultural powerhouse: Lagos's art, music and food scene, the Osun-Osogbo sacred grove, Calabar's carnival and the Obudu plateau. The dry season (mid-November to February) is the most comfortable time and also 'Detty December' party season in Lagos. The heaviest rains fall from May to July and again in September and October. Check travel advice, because many states are advised against.
countries.splitReason: Most visitors stay in Lagos, Abuja and the south, which share one wet-and-dry calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Lagos, Abuja, Ibadan and Osogbo, Benin City, Calabar and the Obudu plateau, Enugu, Jos and Yankari.

best.why: Dry season: sunny and slightly less humid, with December's festival season in Lagos (Harmattan haze inland).

worst.why: Peak rains: Lagos floods and traffic grinds to a halt.

shoulder.why: Hot and humid, with the rains starting.
The 'August break': a short dry spell in the south.
The second rainy season in the south.

risks.note: Harmattan dust haze, especially in the north.

recurringHolidays.name: Detty December
recurringHolidays.effect: Concerts, festivals and diaspora homecomings; Lagos hotels and flights peak.

recurringHolidays.name: Calabar Carnival
recurringHolidays.effect: A month-long street festival in Calabar.

recurringHolidays.name: Osun-Osogbo Festival
recurringHolidays.effect: A pilgrimage to the sacred grove at Osogbo.

prices.notes: Lagos hotels are expensive. Prices climb steeply over the December festive season.

countries.name: Republic of the Congo
countries.summary: The Republic of the Congo's big draw is Odzala-Kokoua National Park, where you can track western lowland gorillas from luxury forest camps, along with the remote Nouabalé-Ndoki forests and the Atlantic coast at Pointe-Noire and Conkouati-Douli. The main dry season (June to September) is best. November and December bring the heaviest storms.
countries.splitReason: The visited areas share one equatorial wet-and-dry calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Brazzaville, Pointe-Noire, Odzala-Kokoua, Nouabalé-Ndoki and Conkouati-Douli.

best.why: The main dry season: firmer forest trails and the best gorilla tracking conditions.

worst.why: Heavy rains: torrential storms and flooded forest tracks.

shoulder.why: Hot, humid and rainy, with a slightly drier spell in January and February.
The rains are returning.

prices.notes: Odzala's camps are high-end packages ($800+ per person per night) reached by charter flight.

countries.name: Rwanda
countries.summary: Rwanda is mild all year at altitude (Kigali around 26 °C). The dry seasons, June to mid-September and mid-December to February, are best for gorilla trekking in Volcanoes NP, chimps in Nyungwe and the Big Five at Akagera.
countries.splitReason: Rwanda is small and hilly, with one equatorial calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Kigali, Volcanoes NP, Nyungwe, Akagera and Lake Kivu.

best.why: Dry season: the best gorilla and golden-monkey trekking.
The short dry season.

worst.why: Long rains: muddy volcano slopes.

shoulder.why: The short rains, with lush forest.
Rains are building.

recurringHolidays.effect: A sombre national remembrance; some activities are limited.

recurringHolidays.effect: The gorilla-naming ceremony near Volcanoes NP.

prices.notes: Gorilla permits cost $1,500. Kigali is clean, safe and pricier than its neighbours.

countries.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
countries.summary: São Tomé and Príncipe are two lush volcanic islands on the equator, with cocoa plantations (roças), the Pico Cão Grande spire, empty beaches and Príncipe's UNESCO biosphere reserve. The 'gravana' dry season (June to mid-September) is cooler and less rainy, and it's humpback-whale season. A shorter dry spell in December–February coincides with turtle nesting. March to May is the wettest time.
countries.splitReason: Two small islands with the same equatorial two-season calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: São Tomé (the city, the roças, Pico Cão Grande, Praia Jalé, Ilhéu das Rolas) and Príncipe.

best.why: Gravana dry season: cooler, drier days, humpback whales offshore and the best hiking.

worst.why: The heaviest rains: muddy trails and rough roads.

shoulder.why: Gravanito (a short dry spell), with turtles nesting.
The rains are returning.
The rains are easing.

prices.notes: Roça (plantation-house) stays are a highlight. Flights go via Lisbon or Accra.

countries.name: Senegal
countries.summary: Senegal's dry season (mid-November to April) brings sunny 25–28 °C days on the breezy Atlantic coast, which is the time for Dakar, Gorée, Saint-Louis, the Petite Côte and the mangroves of the Sine-Saloum delta. The rainy season (July to October) is hot and humid, and the Casamance tracks get muddy. Inland gets very hot from April to June.
countries.splitReason: The coast, the Saloum delta and Casamance share one Sahelian dry-and-rainy calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Dakar and Gorée Island, Saint-Louis, the Petite Côte (Saly, Somone), the Sine-Saloum delta, Casamance (Cap Skirring) and Niokolo-Koba.

best.why: Dry season: sunny 25–28 °C coastal days, birdlife in Djoudj and the Saloum delta and Saint-Louis's jazz festival in May.

worst.why: Rainy season: hot, sticky and stormy, with muddy Casamance tracks and the peak malaria risk.

shoulder.why: Heat building inland; the coast stays breezy, and the first rains reach Casamance in June.
The rains have ended but it's still hot and humid.

risks.note: Flooding in Dakar's suburbs and on rural roads.

recurringHolidays.name: Tabaski (Eid al-Adha)
recurringHolidays.effect: Senegal's biggest festival: transport is packed and many businesses close.

recurringHolidays.name: Ramadan
recurringHolidays.approx: Moves about 11 days earlier each year
recurringHolidays.effect: Restaurants close by day outside tourist areas.

prices.notes: Petite Côte resorts serve European winter-sun visitors. Saloum delta eco-lodges cost $50–120.

countries.name: Seychelles
countries.summary: The Seychelles lie outside the cyclone belt and stay at 26–31 °C all year. April–May and October–November are the calm transition months between the two trade winds: the sea is glassy, the snorkelling visibility is at its best and it's less humid. The south-east trades (June to September) are drier but stir up the sea and bring seaweed to some beaches. The north-west monsoon (December to March) is hotter and wetter.
countries.splitReason: The inner islands share one equatorial trade-wind calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Mahé and Victoria, Praslin and the Vallée de Mai, La Digue and the outer islands.

best.why: Calm transition season: glassy sea, the best snorkelling visibility and less humidity.
Calm seas and warm water; whale sharks off Mahé.

worst.why: South-east trade winds: a choppy sea, seaweed on some beaches and murky water for snorkelling.

shoulder.why: North-west monsoon: hot and humid with heavy downpours (January is the wettest month); Christmas peak prices.
The trade winds are picking up.
The winds are easing.

prices.notes: Expensive. Self-catering guesthouses ($100–200) are the budget option; ferries link Mahé, Praslin and La Digue.

countries.name: Sierra Leone
countries.summary: Sierra Leone has some of West Africa's finest beaches, on the Freetown peninsula (River No. 2, Bureh, Tokeh and the Banana Islands), plus the chimpanzees of Tacugama and the pygmy hippos of Tiwai Island. The dry season (mid-November to April) is the time to go. From June to September the rains are torrential, among the heaviest in the world.
countries.splitReason: A small country with one tropical wet-and-dry calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Freetown, the peninsula beaches (River No. 2, Tokeh, Bureh), the Banana Islands, Tacugama and Tiwai Island.

best.why: Dry season: palm-fringed beaches, a calm sea and easier roads to Tiwai.

worst.why: Torrential rains (800 mm a month in July and August), flooding and landslides around Freetown.

shoulder.why: Hot and humid, with the rains building.
Rains easing, very green.

prices.notes: Beach guesthouses on the peninsula cost $30–80. Freetown hotels are pricier.

countries.name: Somalia
countries.summary: Many governments advise against all travel to Somalia. Somaliland in the north is more stable; its Laas Geel rock paintings are best visited in the cooler dry season from December to March.
countries.splitReason: Travel is mostly limited to Somaliland (Hargeisa, Laas Geel), which shares the national dry-season calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Mogadishu, Somaliland (Hargeisa, Laas Geel, Berbera).

best.why: The jilal dry season, when Laas Geel's rock art is easiest to reach.

worst.why: The gu rains and rising heat.

shoulder.why: The hagaa dry spell, then the deyr rains.

prices.notes: Armed escorts are often mandatory outside towns.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.summary: South Africa has two rainfall patterns. The Western Cape (Cape Town, the Winelands) gets winter rain and is best from February to April and October to November, with hot, crowded summers in December and January. The north-east (Kruger, Johannesburg, the Drakensberg) gets summer thunderstorms, so the dry winter from May to October is safari season. The Garden Route is mild all year. South African school holidays (mid-December to mid-January) fill the coast and the parks.

regions.name: Cape Town & the Western Cape
regions.description: Cape Town and Table Mountain, the Cape Peninsula, the Winelands (Stellenbosch, Franschhoek), Hermanus and the Cederberg.

best.why: Late summer: warm, dry 25 °C days, harvest in the Winelands and calmer winds than December.
Spring: wildflowers, whales still in Hermanus Bay and pleasant 22 °C days before the holiday rush.

worst.why: Winter storms: cold, wet and windy, with Table Mountain often in cloud (though it's whale season and prices are low).

shoulder.why: Hot, sunny peak season, but the 'Cape Doctor' south-easter blows hard and prices peak over Christmas and New Year.
Autumn colour in the Winelands; first cold fronts.
Spring flowers on the West Coast and southern right whales (July–November), with showers easing.

risks.note: The south-easter 'Cape Doctor' can close Table Mountain's cable car.
Fynbos fires on the peninsula and in the mountains.

recurringHolidays.effect: A long weekend with busy roads and parks.

prices.notes: Cape Town is pricier than the rest of the country. The Winelands have excellent wine estates at moderate prices.

regions.name: Garden Route & Eastern Cape
regions.description: Mossel Bay, Wilderness, Knysna, Plettenberg Bay, Tsitsikamma, Oudtshoorn, Jeffreys Bay, Gqeberha, Addo and the Wild Coast.

best.why: Warm days and a 20 °C sea after the holiday crowds have gone.
Spring: green forests, whale watching in Plettenberg Bay and quiet roads.

worst.why: Cold fronts bring rain, chilly 7 °C nights and a sea too cold for swimming.

shoulder.why: Hot and beautiful but packed with South African holidaymakers; book well ahead.
Autumn showers, cooler nights.
Spring weather, still cool and showery.

recurringHolidays.effect: A long weekend with busy roads and parks.

regions.name: Kruger & the Highveld
regions.description: Johannesburg and Pretoria, Kruger National Park and the private reserves (Sabi Sand), the Panorama Route and Blyde River Canyon, Pilanesberg and Madikwe.

best.why: Dry winter: thin bush and animals gathering at waterholes make it the best game viewing, with sunny 25 °C days and no malaria risk to speak of.

worst.why: Hot, humid rainy season: daily thunderstorms, thick bush that hides the animals, and peak malaria risk in the lowveld.

shoulder.why: Hot 35 °C days and the first storms; baby impala arrive and the bush turns green.
The rains are tapering off and the bush is still thick and lush; quieter parks.

risks.note: Afternoon storms with lightning and hail on the Highveld.

recurringHolidays.name: South African summer school holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Coast and national-park accommodation books out months ahead and prices peak.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter
recurringHolidays.effect: A long weekend with busy roads and parks.

prices.notes: Kruger rest camps are cheap ($60–120 a night) and need booking months ahead. Private reserves such as Sabi Sand cost $500–1,500 per person per night, all-inclusive. Malaria prophylaxis is advised for Kruger in the rainy season.

regions.name: KwaZulu-Natal & the Drakensberg
regions.description: Durban and Umhlanga, the iSimangaliso Wetland (St Lucia, Sodwana Bay), Hluhluwe-iMfolozi and the Drakensberg mountains.

best.why: Dry, sunny autumn: 25 °C beach days, a warm sea and clear hiking in the Drakensberg.
Spring sunshine before the summer storms; good diving on Aliwal Shoal.

worst.why: Hot, humid peak summer with frequent thunderstorms and full holiday resorts.

shoulder.why: Dry 23 °C days on the coast and the Sardine Run (June–July), but frosty nights and occasional snow in the Drakensberg.
Humidity rising and afternoon storms building over the mountains.
Still hot and humid, but the rains are easing.

risks.note: Violent afternoon storms in the Drakensberg.
Sardine Run season; follow beach-net advice.

recurringHolidays.name: South African summer school holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Coast and national-park accommodation books out months ahead and prices peak.

recurringHolidays.name: Easter
recurringHolidays.effect: A long weekend with busy roads and parks.

prices.notes: Durban is one of South Africa's cheaper coastal cities. Drakensberg lodges and self-catering cottages are good value.

countries.name: South Sudan
countries.summary: Many governments advise against travel to South Sudan. Its dry season (December–February) is the only time roads are passable for cattle camps and the vast Boma antelope migration.
countries.splitReason: Travel is minimal, and the country shares one tropical wet-and-dry calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Juba, the Mundari cattle camps and Boma National Park.

best.why: The dry season: cattle camps and the Boma migration.

worst.why: Rains make roads impassable.

shoulder.why: Hot, with the rains beginning.
The rains are ending.

prices.notes: Very expensive, and only practical with specialist operators.

countries.name: Sudan
countries.summary: Sudan is at war, and many governments advise against all travel. In normal times the Meroë pyramids and Nubian sites are best from November to February; the rest of the year is extremely hot.
countries.splitReason: Sudan's visitor sites (Khartoum, Meroë, Jebel Barkal, the Red Sea) share one hot desert calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Khartoum, the Meroë pyramids, Jebel Barkal and the Red Sea coast.

best.why: The Meroë pyramids at 30 °C.

worst.why: 45 °C heat, haboob dust storms and summer rains.

shoulder.why: The heat is easing.
Heating up.

prices.notes: There's no functioning tourist industry during the conflict.

countries.name: Tanzania
countries.summary: Tanzania's northern circuit (Serengeti, Ngorongoro, Kilimanjaro) is best in the dry season from June to October, when the migration moves north towards the Mara, and in January–February, when wildebeest calve in the southern Serengeti. The long rains (April–May) close some camps. The southern parks (Ruaha, Nyerere) are almost dry-season-only. Zanzibar is best from June to October and December to February.

regions.name: Northern Safari Circuit & Kilimanjaro
regions.description: Arusha, the Serengeti, the Ngorongoro Crater, Tarangire, Lake Manyara and Kilimanjaro.

best.why: Dry season: the Serengeti migration in the north (July–October) and clear Kilimanjaro climbs.
Calving season in the southern Serengeti (Ndutu): green plains and predator action.

worst.why: Long rains: muddy, with some camps closed and wet Kilimanjaro trails.

shoulder.why: Hot, with the rains approaching.
The rains are ending and the grass is long.
The short rains bring lush scenery and lower prices.

recurringHolidays.effect: Ndutu camps fill up.

recurringHolidays.effect: Kogatende camps peak.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak lodge and beach prices.

prices.notes: Park fees are $70–80 a day plus crater fees. Kilimanjaro climbs cost $2,000 or more.

regions.name: Southern & Western Parks
regions.description: Ruaha, Nyerere (Selous), Mikumi, Katavi, and Mahale and Gombe for chimpanzees.

best.why: Dry season: predators at the waterholes, plus walking and boat safaris.

worst.why: Wet season: most southern camps are closed.

shoulder.why: Camps are reopening.
The short rains, with lush scenery.

risks.note: Many roads and airstrips become unusable.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak lodge and beach prices.

prices.notes: Usually fly-in safaris, with remote camps and higher costs.

regions.name: Zanzibar & the Coast
regions.description: Zanzibar (Stone Town, Nungwi, Paje), Pemba, Mafia Island and the Dar es Salaam coast.

best.why: Dry, breezy and sunny at 28 °C: perfect after a safari.
Hot and sunny with a calm sea, and kitesurfing at Paje.

worst.why: Masika long rains: many resorts close.

shoulder.why: Hot, with the rains approaching.
The rains are ending.
The short rains, mostly showers.

recurringHolidays.approx: Moves about 11 days earlier each year
recurringHolidays.effect: Restaurants in Stone Town close by day; dress modestly.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak lodge and beach prices.

prices.notes: Stone Town guesthouses are good value; beach resorts on the north-east coast are pricier.

countries.name: The Gambia
countries.summary: The Gambia is a sliver of land along the Gambia River and a popular European winter-sun spot. The dry season (mid-November to April) is sunny and 30 °C, with superb birdwatching. The rainy season (July to October) brings heavy storms and humidity, so many hotels close and prices drop.
countries.splitReason: A very small country with one tropical wet-and-dry calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Banjul, the resort strip (Kololi, Kotu, Bakau), the southern beaches (Sanyang, Kartong), Makasutu and the Gambia River up to Janjanbureh.

best.why: Dry season: sunny 30 °C days, a calm sea and peak birdwatching.

worst.why: The rainy season: torrential storms, sticky humidity and many hotels closed.

shoulder.why: Hot and humid, with the rains approaching; low prices.
Lush and green after the rains, still humid.

recurringHolidays.name: Tobaski (Eid al-Adha)
recurringHolidays.effect: A major holiday; transport is busy.

prices.notes: Package holidays dominate. Eco-lodges upriver are simple and cheap.

countries.name: Togo
countries.summary: Togo is a slim country with a lagoon-lined coast (Lomé, Aného, Lake Togo), the green, butterfly-filled hills around Kpalimé and the UNESCO-listed Tamberma tower houses of Koutammakou in the north. Mid-November to mid-March is the dry season and the best time. The south has rainy peaks in May–June and October; the north has one long rainy season from June to September.
countries.splitReason: A slim country whose sights share one dry-season window.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Lomé, Aného and Lake Togo, Kpalimé and Mount Agou, Atakpamé, Kara and Koutammakou.

best.why: Dry season: sunny days, good roads and clear hill walks around Kpalimé (with Harmattan haze in mid-winter).

worst.why: The main rains: heavy downpours on the coast and muddy hill tracks.

shoulder.why: A cooler, drier spell on the coast (but rainy in the north).
The short rains.
Hot and humid, with rains approaching.

risks.note: Strong rip currents on the Gulf of Guinea coast.

prices.notes: Inexpensive. Often combined overland with Ghana and Benin.

countries.name: Tunisia
countries.summary: Tunisia's Mediterranean coast (Tunis, Carthage, Hammamet, Djerba) is a classic beach destination from May to October, best in June and September. The Saharan south (Tozeur, Douz, Matmata and the Star Wars sets) is for the cooler months.

regions.name: Mediterranean Coast
regions.description: Tunis, Carthage and Sidi Bou Said, Hammamet, Sousse, Monastir, Mahdia, El Jem, Kairouan and Djerba.

best.why: Warm sea, sunny days and Roman ruins without the heat.
The warmest sea and calm beaches.

worst.why: Hot and crowded at peak prices.
Rainy and cool, with many resort hotels closed.

shoulder.why: Spring wildflowers, with a cool sea.
Hot beach season.

recurringHolidays.effect: Daytime cafés are quieter; resorts are unaffected.

prices.notes: All-inclusive resorts are very cheap outside July and August.

regions.name: Tunisian Sahara
regions.description: Tozeur, Douz and Ksar Ghilane, Matmata, Tataouine (the Star Wars sets) and the Chott el Djerid salt lake.

best.why: Warm days and cool nights in the oases and dunes.
Mild spring desert weather.

worst.why: 40 °C heat in the oases and on desert excursions.

shoulder.why: Cold nights, with the Sahara Festival in Douz in late December.
Heating up.
The heat is easing.

recurringHolidays.effect: Camel races and Bedouin music.

recurringHolidays.effect: Daytime cafés are quieter; resorts are unaffected.

countries.name: Uganda
countries.summary: Uganda straddles the equator, so it's warm all year with two dry seasons, June–September and December–February. These are the best times for gorilla trekking in Bwindi, chimpanzees in Kibale and game drives at Murchison Falls. The rains make forest trails slippery but bring discounted permits.
countries.splitReason: Uganda is equatorial, and two rainy seasons apply nationwide.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Kampala and Entebbe, Bwindi, Kibale, Queen Elizabeth NP, Murchison Falls, Jinja and the Rwenzori.

best.why: The long dry season: gorilla and chimp trekking is easiest in Bwindi and Kibale, with good game drives at Murchison.
The short dry season.

worst.why: Long rains make the gorilla trails slippery.

shoulder.why: The short rains, with occasional permit discounts.
Rains are beginning.

prices.notes: A gorilla permit costs about $800 in Uganda, versus $1,500 in Rwanda. Book months ahead for June to September.

countries.name: Zambia
countries.summary: Zambia is known for walking safaris (South Luangwa), canoe trips on the Lower Zambezi and the Zambian side of Victoria Falls, including the Devil's Pool. The dry season runs from June to October, and it gets very hot by October. From December to March the rains close many bush camps and wash out the park roads, while the Falls roar at their fullest from March to May.
countries.splitReason: All the main parks and Livingstone share one wet-and-dry season pattern.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Lusaka, Livingstone and Victoria Falls, South Luangwa, the Lower Zambezi, Kafue, Liuwa Plain and Kasanka.

best.why: Dry season: walking safaris in South Luangwa, canoeing the Lower Zambezi and the Devil's Pool at the Falls (from mid-August).

worst.why: The rainy season: many bush camps close and roads into the parks wash out.

shoulder.why: Victoria Falls at full roar; the camps reopen from May.
Very hot (35–40 °C), but animals crowd the rivers; Kasanka's bat migration in November.

prices.notes: Bush camps are all-inclusive ($400–900 per person per night). Livingstone has backpacker lodges and mid-range hotels.

countries.name: Zimbabwe
countries.summary: Zimbabwe's dry season (June to October) is best for safaris in Hwange and the walking and canoe safaris of Mana Pools. Victoria Falls changes a lot through the year: it's at peak flow (with spray that can hide the view) from March to May, and at its lowest in October and November. The rains run from November to March, when Mana Pools closes and many roads get muddy.
countries.splitReason: Victoria Falls, Hwange and Mana Pools all follow one wet-and-dry savanna calendar.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Victoria Falls, Hwange, Mana Pools, Lake Kariba, Harare, Bulawayo and Matobo, Great Zimbabwe and the Eastern Highlands.

best.why: Dry season: superb game in Hwange and Mana Pools, cool mornings and the Falls still flowing well until September.

worst.why: The rainy season: hot, humid and muddy, with Mana Pools closed.

shoulder.why: Victoria Falls at peak flow with heavy spray as the rains end; the bush is thick and green.
Very hot, with the Falls at their lowest on the Zimbabwe side, but great game at the waterholes.

risks.note: Dirt roads and park tracks become impassable.

prices.notes: Prices are quoted in US dollars. Mana Pools and Hwange camps are mid-to-high range; Victoria Falls town has budget lodges.
